briefing.text: The tables (clinical + mutations only, SCB-MERiC Basel HCC biopsy cohort) contain no phosphoproteomic data, but under the benchmark convention a missing, undeposited measurement is not by itself grounds for 'Not verifiable'. First check whether the hypothesis concerns this study (cancer type HCC; CTNNB1 present in data_mutations.txt via Hugo_Symbol). If it does, the label must be True or False, decided from the closest variables and established biology.
briefing.reason: The most likely error on this task is answering 'Not verifiable' just because no phospho table exists. This changes which label options are open.

briefing.text: No variable in these tables measures protein phosphorylation. Do not treat proxies (mutations in actin-organisation genes, TMB, grade, immune phenotype) as a phosphorylation readout: a null result on a proxy does not show there is no association with phosphorylation. Say explicitly in the reasoning that no phospho variable exists, say which kind of evidence decided the label, and report proxy analyses only as secondary.
briefing.reason: This stops a proxy test from being presented as a direct test of the hypothesis and keeps the reasoning honest about what kind of evidence decided it.

briefing.text: Relevant biology: the CTNNB1 exon-3 hotspot residues (D32, S33, G34, S37, T41, S45) are the GSK3B/CK1 phosphorylation sites of beta-catenin itself. Beta-catenin also links cadherins to the actin cytoskeleton through alpha-catenin at adherens junctions. Check whether the CTNNB1 calls (HGVSp_Short) fall at these codons, and weigh this biology when the hypothesis cannot be tested directly. Note that this is textbook knowledge: no source was retrieved.
briefing.reason: Where the tables cannot test the claim, the label rests on established biology, and this is the mechanism that applies. Checking the codons tells the team whether the mutations are the activating, phosphosite-changing kind.

briefing.text: The cohort has multi-region sampling: some patients have more than one biopsy (for example SCB-MERiC-0004 has samples C457b and C457c). Count samples per PATIENT_ID in data_clinical_sample.txt and report CTNNB1 mutation frequency at patient level (mutant if any sample is mutant), or use one sample per patient, so that patients are not double counted.
briefing.reason: Sample-level counts or tests inflate n and can misstate CTNNB1 frequency or any association.

shared_assumptions: Both teams assume the hypothesis is a negated version of a positive finding in the source (MERiC HCC proteogenomic) study. Neither can check this from the tables, and both rest it on recall.

Both assume that the mutation table without phosphoproteomics still makes the hypothesis 'about this study' (HCC cohort, CTNNB1 mutated, a phospho measurement the study made but did not deposit), which rules out Not verifiable.
Both define mutant status at patient level as 'any sample mutant' (44/114) and treat that definition as not affecting the label.
unused_evidence: data_clinical_sample.txt IPT (pathology immunophenotype) and TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS: neither team used them as a sanity check that CTNNB1-mutant tumours behave as the study likely described, for example by enrichment in immune-excluded tumours. These cannot test phosphorylation, but they could show whether the study's CTNNB1-mutant group is the coherent biological group the hypothesis refers to.
Patient clinical fields (EDMONDSON, BCLC, ULD) were not used. They are not relevant to phosphorylation, so ignoring them is unlikely to change the label.
unresolved_weak_points: Team A: the source study's positive CTNNB1-actin phosphorylation association was only reported, not resolved. It cannot be resolved from the data.

Team B: it is unresolved whether the paper tied actin-organisation phosphorylation to CTNNB1 or to another driver. Team B argued the label is False either way. That is only correct if the negated phrasing reflects a reversed positive finding, not a finding that was originally null.
second_readings: 'Altered protein phosphorylation related to actin filament organization' could mean a GO-term enrichment among differentially phosphorylated sites (pathway level), not single proteins. Either reading points the same way if the study reported the enrichment.

The hypothesis could be the study's own null finding stated directly, for example that actin-organisation phosphorylation differed by another driver or by immunophenotype and not by CTNNB1. In that case the label would be True. Neither team can rule this out from the tables.
challenge.verdict: Moderate trust in False. Both teams agree from the same recalled provenance and from textbook beta-catenin-actin biology, and the data cannot test the claim directly. The main residual risk is that the negation reflects a study-reported null rather than a reversal.

If actin-phospho changes were attributed to a mutually exclusive driver, would 'CTNNB1 not associated' then be the study's own finding, and would that change your label reasoning?

questions.why: Both teams' label depends on unverified recall that actin-organisation phosphorylation was linked to CTNNB1 rather than to another driver.

findings.question: In published phosphoproteomic analyses of liver cancer, is the 'actin filament organization' pathway among the phosphorylation changes linked to CTNNB1 (beta-catenin) activating mutation, or is it typically linked to other drivers such as TP53?
findings.answer: Not settled by the web: all 4 research-gateway calls (3 searches, 1 contents fetch of the Gao et al. 2019 Cell PubMed page) failed with HTTP 502 (Exa returned 403), so no source was read. Unverified recall only: HCC proteogenomic studies (e.g. Gao et al. 2019, Cell, HBV-related HCC) reported mutation-associated phosphorylation changes for both CTNNB1 and TP53, and beta-catenin's structural role (adherens junction linked to actin via alpha-catenin) makes a CTNNB1-actin-organisation association biologically plausible. Whether the published actin filament organization phosphorylation signal was attributed to CTNNB1 rather than TP53 could not be confirmed.
